discovery: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class of kinetic roughening and its experimental confirmation
motivation: In 1986 Kardar and Zhang, with Giorgio Parisi, proposed a nonlinear stochastic equation for growing interfaces. It became the central paradigm of non-equilibrium scaling. The KPZ equation predicts universal roughness exponents, and it was later shown to predict universal Tracy-Widom fluctuation distributions for flame fronts, bacterial colonies, burning paper, directed polymers in random media, Burgers turbulence and, more recently, quantum spin chains and exciton-polariton condensates. Takeuchi's liquid-crystal turbulence experiments (2010-2012) gave the first precise quantitative confirmation of these exact predictions. They included the curved and flat geometry-dependent distributions and fixed a long-debated theory to exceptional accuracy. Together, this work shows that universality holds far from equilibrium and in disordered, driven matter, not only at equilibrium critical points. Parisi has already been honoured for other work. KPZ physics now links statistical mechanics, integrable probability and condensed matter, and its originators and chief experimental verifier deserve recognition.
